items.headline: TSMC posts record Q3 profit (net income up 69% to roughly $24B) but U.S. shares fall 4.14% as gross margin slips to 66.4% from 67.7%
items.why: Record profit failing to lift the stock on a margin dip shows the market is now pricing the quality of AI capex, not just its headline growth.

items.why: It is one of the first widely-cited estimates of how much of the current AI buildout could end up as stranded capital — a useful counterweight to pure growth narratives.

items.headline: September FOMC minutes (released Oct 7) show a unanimous 12-0 hike to 3.75%-4.00%, with most officials saying another hike 'would likely be appropriate by year end'
items.why: Markets had been leaning toward cuts; a unanimous hawkish vote resets the baseline every other asset in this brief has been reacting to this week.

items.headline: A hot September CPI print and PPI (+6.3% y/y, the largest gain since 2022) pushed next-meeting hike odds to roughly a coin flip, before an afternoon pullback in Treasury yields (10-year -10.5bp to 5.085%) helped stocks pare their losses
items.why: The intraday reversal shows how sensitive the tape now is to yield moves layered on top of the inflation data itself.

items.headline: Gold slipped 0.83% to $4,181.50 on Oct 12 as WTI crude gained 1.59% to $93.31, both tracking the firmer-dollar, higher-yield backdrop from the hawkish Fed minutes
items.why: Gold falling while yields and the dollar firm is the textbook rates-driven move rather than a safe-haven one.

items.headline: A gold-mine restart study filed Oct 14 pegs after-tax project value at $181M using a $3,000/oz gold price, rising to $439M at $4,000/oz
items.why: Mine-economics studies like this show what price level the industry itself is underwriting new supply at, a useful real-world anchor for where miners expect gold to settle.
